# Tiles snap to each other, not to a grid

Tiles snap magnetically to the edges and corners of nearby tiles and of the mat, and inside the rectangle every position is some number of x's plus some number of units from the corner of the T. There is deliberately no grid. A unit grid would force an x tile to be a whole number of units long, and students who lay unit tiles beside it would conclude that x equals that number, the misconception physical tile sets avoid by making x a length no number of units matches. Don't "fix" snapping by adding a grid.
